'''''Cotula coronopifolia''''' is a [[species]] of [[flower|flowering]] plant in the aster [[Family (botany)|family]] ([[Asteraceae]]). Commonly known as '''brass buttons''', '''golden buttons''', and '''buttonweed''', it is native to southern [[Africa]].<ref>https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:198443-1</ref>

==Description==
The [[flower heads]] are bright yellow [[discoid head|discoid]] heads that look like thick buttons. Individual plants spread stems along the ground and send up the knobby flowers at intervals. The plant is native to southern Africa, but it has been introduced to other parts of the world ([[Europe]], [[North America|North]] + [[South America]], etc.).<ref name=emily>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=220003387 Flora of North America, Brass-buttons, cotule, Cotula coronopifolia Linnaeus, Sp. Pl. 2: 892. 1753. ]</ref><ref>Turner, B. L. 1996. The Comps of Mexico: A systematic account of the family Asteraceae, vol. 6. Tageteae and Athemideae. Phytologia Memoirs 10: i–ii, 1–22, 43–93.</ref><ref>Welsh, S. L. 1974. Anderson's Flora of Alaska and Adjacent Parts of Canada i–xvi, 1–724. Brigham Young University Press, Provo</ref><ref>Marticorena, C. & M. Quezada. 1985. Catálogo de la Flora Vascular de Chile. Gayana, Botánica 42: 1–157</ref><ref>Gibbs Russell, G. E., W. G. M. Welman, E. Retief, K. L. Immelman, G. Germishuizen, B. J. Pienaar, M. Van Wyk & A. Nicholas. 1987. List of species of southern African plants. Memoirs of the Botanical Survey of South Africa  2(1–2): 1–152(pt. 1), 1–270(pt. 2).</ref><ref>[https://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=cotula+coronopifolia Altervista Flora Italiana, Margherita sudafricana, ''Cotula coronopifolia'' L.] includes photos and European distribution map</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Stace |first=Clive |title=New Flora of the British Isles |publisher=C & M Floristics |year=2019 |isbn=9781527226302 |edition=4th |location=Middlewood Green, Suffolk |pages=798–799}}</ref>

Brass buttons are common plants that occupy a specialized [[ecological niche]]. They prefer muddy, [[Anoxic waters|anoxic]] [[wetland]]s and [[brackish water]]. They are very salt-tolerant. The plant has fat, fleshy leaves that store water during times of saline inundation. The reddish stems and green, blade-shaped leaves are coated with a shiny cuticle to retain moisture. It can also be found in the wetter patches in [[vernal pool]] ecosystems. Brass buttons are common along beaches, [[salt marsh]]es, and estuaries from [[California]] to [[Washington (state)|Washington]].<ref name=emily/><ref>[https://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Cotula%20coronopifolia.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref> It has been present in the British Isles since the late 1800s, especially on the [[Cheshire]] coast and is considered a [[Neophyte (botany)|neophyte]] naturalised plant.

Although brass buttons is known to be [[Invasive species in the United States|invasive]], its spread appears to be relatively slow. Its California Invasive Plant Council Inventory rating is "limited",<ref>[https://www.cal-ipc.org/ip/management/plant_profiles/Cotula_coronopifolia.php California Invasive Plant Council plant profile: ''Cotula coronopifolia'' (brassbuttons) Accessed Dec. 19, 2013]</ref> that is, "invasive but their ecological impacts are minor on a statewide level or there was not enough information to justify a higher score. Their reproductive biology and other attributes result in low to moderate rates of invasiveness. Ecological amplitude and distribution are generally limited, but these species may be locally persistent and problematic."<ref>[https://www.cal-ipc.org/ip/inventory/index.php#definitions California Invasive Plant Inventory  Accessed Dec. 19, 2013]</ref>
